questions.stem: According to the passage, what did a recent U.S. government study find?
options: About 1 in 17 adults in the United States have been diagnosed with ADHD.
About 1 in 17 children in the United States have been diagnosed with ADHD.
More than 7 million adults have been diagnosed with ADHD.
Half of all children with ADHD are diagnosed as adults.
questions.evidence: A recent government study suggested that more than 15 million adults in the United States — about 1 in 17 — have been diagnosed with ADHD.
questions.explanation_ko: 본문에서 정부 연구는 성인의 약 17명 중 1명이 ADHD 진단을 받았다고 밝혔습니다.

questions.stem: According to the passage, all of the following are mentioned in connection with diagnosing ADHD EXCEPT:
options: A blood or brain test for the disorder
Getting careful histories from patients and people who know them
Testing a patient's memory and ability to focus
Online diagnostic tests linked to companies that prescribe medication
questions.evidence: There is no blood or brain test for the disorder.
questions.explanation_ko: 본문은 ADHD를 진단할 혈액이나 뇌 검사는 없다고 명시했으므로, 이는 진단 방법으로 언급되지 않았습니다.

questions.stem: What can be inferred about people with less severe ADHD symptoms during the COVID-19 pandemic?
options: Their symptoms may have become more noticeable due to pandemic conditions like working from home with children.
They were less likely to seek diagnosis because clinics were closed.
Their symptoms disappeared once schools reopened.
They were diagnosed at the same rate as before the pandemic.
questions.evidence: She said such conditions may have worsened ADHD symptoms in people with less severe cases.
questions.explanation_ko: 팬데믹으로 인한 재택근무와 육아 상황이 경미한 ADHD 증상을 악화시켜 더 눈에 띄게 만들었을 것이라고 추론할 수 있습니다.

questions.stem: Why does the author include Judy Sandler's quote about feeling like she has "an engine" inside her?
options: To give a personal, vivid description of what living with ADHD feels like.
To argue that medication is the only effective treatment for ADHD.
To compare Sandler's experience with that of children diagnosed with ADHD.
To explain the scientific cause of ADHD symptoms.
questions.evidence: “It’s like there’s an engine in you and you feel like it’s always running, and you can’t turn it off except with medication,” Sandler said.
questions.explanation_ko: 이 인용문은 ADHD를 겪는 사람의 개인적이고 생생한 경험을 전달하기 위해 사용되었습니다.

questions.stem: In the sentence "The disorder was once thought to be something that resolved as children became adults," the word "resolved" most nearly means:
options: went away
became worse
changed completely
was diagnosed
questions.evidence: The disorder was once thought to be something that resolved as children became adults.

blanks.sentence_ko: "저는 이것이 제가 겪고 있는 문제일 수도 있다는 것을 짜맞출 수 있었어요," 버크가 말했다.
일부 의사들은 ADHD 검사를 받으려는 사람들의 수가 급격히 증가하고 있다고 말한다.
"이 나라에서는 사람들이 얼마나 엄격하게, 누구를 진단하는지에 있어서 폭넓은 차이가 있습니다," 시블리가 말했다.
전문가들은 오랫동안 성인의 ADHD가 과소 진단되었다고 믿어왔다고 말한다.

key_points: ADHD diagnoses have risen sharply among both adults and children over the past two decades, with a notable increase in recent years.
A recent U.S. government study found about 1 in 17 adults have been diagnosed with ADHD, and about half of adults with ADHD are diagnosed at 18 or older.
Experts attribute the rise partly to a 2013 change in diagnostic criteria that expanded the definition of ADHD and lowered the number of required symptoms.
The COVID-19 pandemic, with school closures and remote work, appears to have worsened symptoms and increased diagnoses, especially among women.
There is no blood or brain test for ADHD; diagnosis relies on patient histories, memory/focus tests, and observed symptoms across multiple areas of life.
Experts now debate whether ADHD, once thought underdiagnosed in adults, may now be overdiagnosed, and diagnostic practices vary widely across the country.
main_idea: ADHD diagnoses among adults and children in the United States have risen sharply in recent years due to factors like changed diagnostic criteria and pandemic-related stress, prompting debate over whether the disorder is now overdiagnosed and highlighting inconsistencies in how it is diagnosed.
restate_sentence: Those changes expanded the definition of ADHD and reduced the number of signs, or symptoms, required for diagnosis.
